- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience or mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overreacts and forecasts continued ascent; cap upward momentum after peak.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to early forecast values.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.6 to -0.6 within 5 days), model lags in adjusting; shift forecast downward 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- Model tends to overfit recent volatility; if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility, reduce forecast sensitivity to short-term noise.
- When sentiment is flat or mixed (0.0–0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply slight downward bias to mid-term forecasts.
